source: Jiang, Li, Qian, Zhang, Luo (2025) AutoTRIZ: Automating Engineering Innovation with TRIZ and LLMs
finding: AutoTRIZ is a four-module GPT-4 pipeline that mirrors classic TRIZ: restate problem, find the engineering contradiction, look up principles in the 39x39 matrix, write solutions.
numbers: Modules 1, 2, 4 are LLM-driven; module 3 (matrix lookup) is a fixed table, not the LLM.
limits: Only 10 textbook cases and one battery-cooling case study; no controlled human comparison of idea quality.
agent_relevance: A fixed-table step inside an LLM chain is a template for typed reframes (O4/O8): the model names the parameters, code fetches the principles.

source: Jiang, Li, Qian, Zhang, Luo (2025) AutoTRIZ: Automating Engineering Innovation with TRIZ and LLMs
finding: Contradiction detection is unstable across repeated runs. 100 runs per problem gave a spread of different parameter pairs.
numbers: Entropy scale 0 to 6.64 (100 runs). 7 of 10 cases matched or half-matched the textbook contradiction inside the top 3 detections. Only cases 5, 6, 7, 8 had a dominant top answer (two complete matches). In almost all cases one parameter stayed fixed while the other varied.
limits: Textbook analysis is not a gold standard (authors say so). Top-3 scoring is lenient. N=10 cases.
agent_relevance: Sample the reframe several times and vote, or keep the spread. High-probability outputs matched experts best, so frequency is a usable confidence signal.

source: Jiang, Li, Qian, Zhang, Luo (2025) AutoTRIZ: Automating Engineering Innovation with TRIZ and LLMs
finding: Asking plain ChatGPT to use TRIZ in chat gave visible errors; the structured pipeline avoided them in the authors' view.
numbers: Qualitative only: no error rate given.
quote: always included apparent errors, such as mismatched contradictions and inventive principles
limits: Anecdote by the authors, not a measured comparison. An author-side expert checked results.
agent_relevance: Scaffolds that fix step order beat free chat for a method with a lookup table; but no number backs it.

source: Jiang, Li, Qian, Zhang, Luo (2025) AutoTRIZ: Automating Engineering Innovation with TRIZ and LLMs
finding: Real design application: AutoTRIZ principles IP7 nesting, IP17 new dimension, IP35 state change led to a flat-heat-pipe battery thermal design checked by simulation.
numbers: Versus best prior schemes: grouping efficiency +24%, energy density +64%, thermal management efficiency +26% (authors' calculation). Efficiency 43% vs 33-34%.
limits: One case; a co-author expert verified the output; no blind control without TRIZ.
agent_relevance: Shows a principle-guided prompt can seed a real, testable design. Not proof that TRIZ added value over plain prompting.

source: Jiang, Li, Qian, Zhang, Luo (2025) AutoTRIZ: Automating Engineering Innovation with TRIZ and LLMs
finding: Authors name limits: only 40 principles; they suggest combining with other ideation methods to widen the space; hints on improvement direction in the input help match experts.
numbers: Case base 10 problems from 7 textbooks.
limits: Wider expert comparison of novelty, usefulness and breadth is left to future work.
agent_relevance: Matches the Fiorineschi point that one method gives non-comprehensive creativity support: keep several reframe operators, not one.

source: Chen, Song, Ding, Sun, Childs, Zuo (2024) TRIZ-GPT: An LLM-augmented method for problem-solving
finding: Four prompt strategies tested on TRIZ contradiction analysis with GPT-4. Plain and chain-of-thought prompts recalled the literature contradictions best; few-shot made recall collapse.
numbers: 34 cases (37 classic minus 3 used for few-shot). Recall/precision: basic 0.675/0.259; CoT 0.691/0.310; few-shot 0.245/0.333; CoT+few-shot 0.247/0.298.
limits: Recall only checks whether the textbook pair appears among many generated pairs; precision is low by design. Low temperature for this step.
agent_relevance: Few-shot examples narrowed the model to the example pattern and hurt coverage: for reframing, prefer a short reasoning path over examples.

source: Chen, Song, Ding, Sun, Childs, Zuo (2024) TRIZ-GPT: An LLM-augmented method for problem-solving
finding: For solution reasoning from given principles, prompt strategy did not matter.
numbers: Cosine similarity to literature solutions: base M=0.829 SD=0.031; CoT 0.823 SD=0.031; few-shot 0.824 SD=0.030; CoT+few-shot 0.824 SD=0.033. No significant differences reported.
limits: Embedding similarity to a textbook answer rewards sameness, not novelty. Principles came from the literature, so this tests only the application step.
agent_relevance: Once the principle is chosen, the prompt wrapper adds little. The leverage is upstream, in choosing the contradiction.

source: Chen, Song, Ding, Sun, Childs, Zuo (2024) TRIZ-GPT: An LLM-augmented method for problem-solving
finding: GPT-4 beats GPT-3.5 on contradiction recall at equal prompts and infers more parameter pairs.
numbers: Post-April-2023 case set (10 cases, outside GPT-4 training). Recall GPT-4 0.544 vs GPT-3.5 0.400 (basic and CoT); few-shot 0.288 vs 0.304; CoT+few-shot 0.275 vs 0.383. GPT-3.5 precision higher in few-shot rows (0.483, 0.513).
limits: Small N; no significance test for the model comparison. Table 2 differs from Table 1 because it uses a different case set.
agent_relevance: A weaker model gains from few-shot structure while a strong one does not. Test the scaffold on the model that will run the agent.

source: Chen, Song, Ding, Sun, Childs, Zuo (2024) TRIZ-GPT: An LLM-augmented method for problem-solving
finding: GPT-4 was stable in contradiction reasoning across repeats on most cases.
numbers: Consistent reasoning for at least some repeats in 85.3% of cases (basic prompt) and 88.2% (CoT prompt).
limits: Consistency means the literature contradiction recurred, not that it is right.
agent_relevance: Supports using a TRIZ-style reframe as a repeatable operator.

source: Chen, Song, Ding, Sun, Childs, Zuo (2024) TRIZ-GPT: An LLM-augmented method for problem-solving
finding: The authors added recent cases to reduce training contamination.
numbers: 37 classic cases plus 10 cases published after April 2023.
limits: Classic cases are likely in training data; the share of recall that is memory is not quantified.
agent_relevance: Any TRIZ test for our agent needs post-cutoff or private problems.

source: Mohammadi, Zeng (2025) Enhancing TRIZ through Environment-Based Design supported by an LLM
finding: Environment-Based Design questions, interaction network and functional analysis (GPT-3.5 prompts in LangChain) feed a TRIZ idea step that loops 40 times, once per principle.
numbers: 12 prompts; idea prompt loops 40 times; temperature 1 for creativity.
limits: GPT-3.5 only. Three design problems from TRIZ literature.
agent_relevance: Closest published case of TRIZ inside an LLM loop with an explicit problem-definition stage before the contradiction. It repairs the problem-framing gap in front of TRIZ.

source: Mohammadi, Zeng (2025) Enhancing TRIZ through Environment-Based Design supported by an LLM
finding: Generated questions and interaction extraction scored high against two EBD experts; functional analysis accuracy was about 50 percent.
numbers: Table 6 (3 cases, 2 evaluators): question accuracy 0.77 to 1; question comprehensiveness 0.82 to 0.91; interaction scores 0.90 to 0.97. Table 9 functional-analysis accuracy 0.56, 0.59, 0.58 (LLM) with expert-reference values 0.35, 0.41, 0.27.
limits: Two graduate-student evaluators; case 1 comprehensiveness not computable; reference is a published textbook solution.
agent_relevance: LLM problem-structuring is checkable but only about half right. A verify step is needed before the contradiction is trusted.

source: Mohammadi, Zeng (2025) Enhancing TRIZ through Environment-Based Design supported by an LLM
finding: LLM-TRIZ produced more ideas, more variety and mostly higher novelty than TRIZ experts' textbook solutions, with a wide quality spread.
numbers: Table 8 (Shah et al. metrics). Ideas LLM vs expert: case 1 20 vs 4; case 2 7 vs 2; case 3 18 vs 1 or 2. Variety e.g. 34 vs 12, 31 vs 7, 16 vs 4, 13 vs 9, 24 vs 1.5, 40 vs 6.5. Novelty mean 2.42 vs 2, 3.41 vs 2.56, 2.13 vs 1.77, 1.49 vs 2.07 (expert higher), 2.79 vs 1.43, 3.32 vs 2.57.
limits: Counts favour a model that generates on demand; textbooks print few ideas (authors admit this bias). Duplicates removed by hand. No feasibility score.
agent_relevance: Wide, cheap generation per principle fills the quantity and variety gap; quality filtering must follow. One of six novelty comparisons went to the human.

source: Mohammadi, Zeng (2025) Enhancing TRIZ through Environment-Based Design supported by an LLM
finding: Authors link to Ma et al. 2023: plain GPT-3 ideas were more feasible and less novel than human ones; their TRIZ-structured model was more novel than experts.
numbers: Quality judged by two experts; spread from irrelevant ideas to some better than expert ones.
limits: Different models and baselines; not a controlled test of TRIZ against plain prompting.
agent_relevance: Suggests structure may buy novelty while a plain prompt buys feasibility. Needs a same-model, same-problem test.

source: Szczepanik, Chudziak (2025) TRIZ Agents: A Multi-Agent LLM Approach for TRIZ-Based Innovation
finding: A project-manager agent plus specialist agents (TRIZ specialist, mechanical, control, safety, electrical) ran a six-step TRIZ workflow on a gantry-crane case with RAG and web tools (GPT-4o).
numbers: Compared step by step with one published case study. Physical contradictions found 'exactly the same'. Two engineering contradictions (speed vs stability, load capacity vs safety) near but not equal to the paper's.
limits: One case, no scores, no plain GPT-4o baseline. Qualitative comparison by the authors.
agent_relevance: First published TRIZ multi-agent loop. The matrix step is deterministic code.

source: Szczepanik, Chudziak (2025) TRIZ Agents: A Multi-Agent LLM Approach for TRIZ-Based Innovation
finding: Fidelity to the human case was partial: some function links and one solution were missed.
numbers: Six useful connections from the case study not found; worker-system harmful link missed; 5 extra root causes (logical) beyond the 2 in the case. Sliding mode control matched; intelligent circuit breaker missed because the electrical agent was never called.
limits: Single case. 'Not found' may mean the case study was incomplete.
agent_relevance: Routing matters: a specialist never invoked leaves a solution class unexplored. Add a coverage check over roles.

source: Szczepanik, Chudziak (2025) TRIZ Agents: A Multi-Agent LLM Approach for TRIZ-Based Innovation
finding: Authors report two weaknesses: no feedback loop (the manager never sent the team back to a step) and heavy dependence on agent profile prompts.
numbers: The TRIZ specialist rarely used the RAG tool; many prompt iterations were needed before the team followed the workflow.
quote: the outcome of the system strongly depends on agents' profiling prompts
limits: No numbers; design limitation noted by authors.
agent_relevance: Our schema has revisit states; TRIZ run as a one-way pipeline loses the repair loop.

source: Wang, Uzzi (2026) Inventive Problem Solving with LLMs: A Benchmark for TRIZ Reasoning (TRIZBench)
finding: TRIZBench is a patent-grounded benchmark with three tasks: contradiction prediction, inventive principle prediction, grounded TRIZ reasoning.
numbers: Abstract only: spotting a contradiction is easier than naming the right trade-off pair; principle prediction improves when models use TRIZ structure explicitly; semantic retrieval helps ground justifications and explains failures. 18 pages. No scores in the abstract.
limits: I read the abstract page only; the GitHub README gave no numbers. Do not quote accuracies from this paper.
agent_relevance: Direct test bed for a typed-reframe operator. Next step: pull the data and run an equal-token test.

source: Wang, Uzzi (2026) TRIZBench repository
finding: Code and data released (data folder, patent_parameters.csv).
numbers: 7 commits and 2 stars at fetch time.
limits: README text not retrievable; contents unverified.
agent_relevance: Usable for our own measurement.

source: Trapp, Warschat (2024) LLM-based Extraction of Contradictions from Patents
finding: Zero-shot gpt-4-1106 extracted TRIZ contradictions from patent text, but the headline 0.93 is a text-similarity score, not sentence accuracy.
numbers: 100 patents with PaGAN contradictions: sentence recall 0.71 (2.69 of 3.81 found), precision 0.46, F1 0.56; 3.19 false-positive sentences per patent. BERTScore-F1 0.93 (concatenated sentences) and 0.88 (summary).
limits: PaGAN annotations may be incomplete. Third-party summaries quoted 0.93 as the F1.
agent_relevance: Report the strict metric. The loose one hides that the model finds the right region but over-extracts.

source: Trapp, Warschat (2024) LLM-based Extraction of Contradictions from Patents
finding: GPT-4 matched or slightly beat the best fine-tuned sentence classifiers on the same task.
numbers: Zero-shot F1 0.56 vs best PaTRIZ classifier weighted F1 0.54 (0.37 and 0.65 for its two parts); full PaTRIZ pipeline precision 0.33.
limits: Different splits; 100-patent sample; no significance test.
agent_relevance: A prompt-only reframe step can match trained systems at contradiction spotting.

source: Trapp, Warschat (2024) LLM-based Extraction of Contradictions from Patents
finding: On patents the annotators called contradiction-free, GPT-4 still found contradictions in 86 of 100.
numbers: Mean 4.84 sentences extracted per such patent vs 5.88 in the positive set; the authors argue a golf-ball patent was mislabelled.
limits: Either the model over-detects or the annotators under-label; the paper does not decide.
agent_relevance: A typed-reframe operator will see conflicts everywhere. It needs a rejection rule or the agent will always find a trade-off.

source: Ma, Grandi, McComb, Goucher-Lambert (2023) Conceptual Design Generation Using Large Language Models
finding: Plain GPT-3 (davinci-003) solutions to 12 design problems were rated more feasible and useful but less novel than crowdsourced human solutions.
numbers: 12 problems, 100 solutions each from the crowd and from GPT-3; 600 solutions expert-rated (20 per prompt subsample); two experts, Cohen's kappa fair to moderate.
limits: GPT-3 only; solutions repeat with small changes; crowd workers, not engineers.
agent_relevance: Sets the no-method baseline TRIZ-style scaffolds must beat: feasibility high, novelty low.

source: Ma, Grandi, McComb, Goucher-Lambert (2023) Conceptual Design Generation Using Large Language Models
finding: Prompt wording changes diversity: few-shot examples pull LLM solutions toward the crowd set; adding 'diverse' or 'unique' pushes them away.
numbers: Mean embedding similarity to crowd set: few-shot 0.804 (SD 0.06), zero-shot with 'unique' 0.746 (SD 0.06). Per-problem cells range 0.627 to 0.869; one 'diverse' prompt fell from 0.738 to 0.675.
limits: Large per-problem variation (SD up to 0.12); few samples; embedding similarity.
agent_relevance: Few-shot examples reduce divergence, same direction as the TRIZ-GPT few-shot recall drop.

source: Zhu, Luo (2022) Generative Pre-Trained Transformer for Design Concept Generation: An Exploration
finding: Early test of GPT-2 and GPT-3 for verbal design concepts, problem-driven and analogy-driven.
numbers: Abstract: both models give 'reasonably good performance'; Ma et al. say it produced 500 GPT-3 solutions.
limits: Early models; I read the abstract and introduction only.
agent_relevance: Pre-history of LLM ideation; no TRIZ element.

source: Sankar, Sen (2024) A Novel Idea Generation Tool using a Structured Conversational AI System
finding: Pilot with 30 postgraduate design students: GPT ideas were preferred to designer ideas in pairwise votes by 20 expert designers; classic techniques in the study included SCAMPER, Synectics, brainstorming, random words.
numbers: 68% of experts judged the GPT statements more meaningful (Figure 5a).
limits: Pilot, 30 participants in six groups; choosing ideas stayed with the humans.
agent_relevance: An LLM beats classic creativity techniques in a pairwise vote at low N; selection stays human.

source: Chen, Tsang, Jing, Sun (2024) LLM-augmented morphological analysis for conceptual design (DRS 2024)
finding: Three-arm design: manual morphological analysis, unstructured GPT-4 chat, proposed LLM-augmented morphology. A secondary summary reports gains in creativity and lower workload.
numbers: No numbers verified.
limits: Not opened; the download returned an HTML page, and only a blog summary was seen.
agent_relevance: Closest LLM work to the systematic-design half (morphological chart). Open the paper before using.

source: Fiorineschi, Frillici, Rotini (2018) Integrating TRIZ with systematic design
finding: Key work of this subfield. A search for Fiorineschi plus LLM concept evaluation found no LLM test of it, only a citation of their 2018 and 2021 work in the Mohammadi paper.
numbers: None read here (other angles cover the paper).
limits: Not opened by this angle. Gap: no LLM test of TRIZ combined with systematic design found.
agent_relevance: The combined method (functional decomposition then TRIZ) has not been tested on an LLM; our test would be new.

source: IdeaForge (2026) knowledge-graph-grounded multi-agent innovation analysis (authors not recorded)
finding: A multi-agent system with TRIZ, Design Thinking and SCAMPER agents links claims supported by two or more methods as CONVERGENT and ranks them by InnovationScore (weight 0.4 on convergent count).
numbers: Five domains, all on TinyLlama via Ollama, threshold 0.65; 16 nodes and 3 claims each. 4 of 5 domains had 3 convergent pairs; sepsis had 1. Top scores 0.500, 0.353, 0.500, 0.467, 0.500.
limits: Tiny model, no human rating, no numeric baseline; single-method comparison given in words only. Score is a heuristic.
agent_relevance: Multi-method agreement as a confidence signal is testable and addresses the non-comprehensive support of one method. Evidence is only illustrative.
